name: Warren Hills

climate.koppen_name: Cold, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Riesling, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon and Cabernet Franc fully without cooking off their freshness.

soil.rock: Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen. Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 2°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
